ac.description: One 1050 W AC supply, two front-to-back fan modules and covers on the empty slots, the switch as shipped. The slot also takes the 1600 W supply.

dual-psu.description: The EX4400-24P with a second 1050 W supply in slot 1, for the 1+1 redundancy the guide describes. An illustration, not an order code.

em-4y.description: The EX4400-24P as shipped, with an EX4400-EM-4Y extension module in the extension slot in place of the cover. An illustration, not an order code.

s.description: The spare chassis EX4400-24P-S. It ships with no power supply and no fan modules, and they are ordered separately. The guide lists 2000 W DC as its supply and the AFO fan module.

description: Juniper EX4400-24P campus access switch, 1RU. It has 24 10/100/1000BASE-T RJ-45 ports with IEEE 802.3bt PoE of up to 90 W per port. The front also holds a USB-C console port, the chassis and port mode lamps, a mode button and one extension module slot. The rear holds two 100GbE QSFP28 ports, console, management and USB-A ports, two fan modules and two power supply slots. A shipped switch carries one supply, two front-to-back fan modules and covers on the empty slots. The default configuration names a 1050 W AC supply, and the -S spare ships with no supply and no fans.

gaps.note: The jack part gives led-a the vocabulary link and led-b the vocabulary activity. This switch's right lamp is a status lamp whose meaning follows the mode button, and the upper row is rotated so left and right swap. One group mapping cannot say both.
gaps.wanted: A per-port states mapping that a block can carry, or the jack part split by row.

gaps.note: The hardware guide names the CLD lamp and sends the reader to the cloud-ready LED blink patterns, which are not in this guide.
gaps.wanted: the cloud-ready LED blink patterns and their meanings

gaps.note: The HPE datasheet a00150783enw did not answer from this host, so no datasheet is cited and no figure comes from it.
gaps.wanted: the HPE PSNow EX4400 datasheet, for the ordering part numbers and mounting kit codes

gaps.note: Table 53 gives the 1050 and 1600 W supplies a C15 coupler, which mates a C16 appliance inlet. The registry has only the C14 inlet, which the supply parts use, so the C16 rim is not drawn and a C13 cord would also fit the drawing.
gaps.wanted: a C16 inlet in the connector registry

gaps.note: Table 9 prints "100/1000BASE-X ports: 36" as the built-in ports of the EX4400-24P, a row that matches the EX4400-48F's table and not this switch. The same topic's front figure (Figure 4), its callout list (Figure 6, "10/100/1000BASE-T ports"), the opening sentence ("24 RJ-45 ports that support PoE-bt") and Table 114 (PIC 0, 24 ports) all give 24 RJ-45 ports. The 24 RJ-45 ports are modelled and the table row is not used.

The spare chassis takes the 2000 W DC supply, juniper/jpsu-2000-c-dc-afo. The guide draws its face only in perspective (Figure 85), so the right half of the face is placed by eye and is estimated. The guide also prints the supply's model number two ways, with and without the C, and the form with the C is used.
gaps.wanted: a render or photograph of the 2000 W DC supply's face

gaps.note: The guide prints EX4400-FAN once, in the switch-tray assembly table, with no airflow direction. No ordering code is stated for the fan modules.
gaps.wanted: the ordering codes of the front-to-back and back-to-front fan modules

gaps.note: The guide states the screw size and lug codes but not the spacing of the two grounding holes. The 15.0 mm spacing is estimated from the render. The holes are drawn as decor, so no two-hole lug can be seated on them.
gaps.wanted: the spacing of the two-hole protective earthing terminal, and a 10-32 pair part for it

gaps.note: The guide sends the reader to the Hardware Compatibility Tool page for EX4400 for the transceivers and cables each port takes, and holds no table of them. The port groups therefore declare no interface.
gaps.wanted: the EX4400 transceiver list from the Hardware Compatibility Tool

gaps.note: The ESD hazard symbol beside the ESD socket and the legends printed on the fan and power supply slot plates are drawn as simple marks. The air-flow word printed on the supply fan hub in the community elevation is not drawn, because no maker figure shows it.

mgmt.mixed: reaching and restarting the switch - USB-C console and mode button on the front, RJ-45 console and management, USB-A and the reset pinhole on the rear

attrs.redundancy-note: Two slots, one supply shipped. The guide says a second supply gives full redundancy and that supplies of different ratings must not be mixed

qsfp28.description: Two rear ports numbered 0 and 1. They are Virtual Chassis ports by default and can run as network ports. Each takes a 100G or a 40G transceiver

qsfp28-leds.description: Four lamps for each QSFP28 port, in two rows of two. Table 46 - green for 100G, amber for 40G, and all four lamps show the four channels of a channelized port

rj45.description: 24 ports, numbered 0 to 23 as printed, upper jack of each column even. Each port runs at 10, 100 or 1000 Mbps

status-leds.description: the chassis status and port mode lamps at the right of the front panel

name: ex4400-24p

airflow.note: Table 8 and Table 10 - the 24P ships only with front-to-back (AFO) fan modules and supply (AIR OUT label, orange handle). No back-to-front 24P is listed anywhere in the guide. The -S spare ships with no supply and no fan modules, and the guide says the fans to order are AFO.

colour.note: Median of bare face on the guide renders (#777777 at the front, #707070 at the rear), and of the status plate (#50575f) and the jack plate (#cccdcf). The 24X studio photograph shows the same mid-grey finish. The legends of the PoE models are gold (#e8a626) on the render.

extension-slot.note: Figure 6 callout 6. The slot is a recess 363.8 to 437.8 across and 17.7 to 41.2 down in the render of Figure 4. The slot is a bay. It takes the three extension modules the guide names and ships with a cover, because Table 105 lists one cover for the empty extension module slot. The modules are not part of this device.

gate-1.note: Both renders pass at low resolution. Figure 4 (g022642, 1500 x 199 px, embedded image extracted from the PDF) gives a face 1298 px wide and 127.5 px tall, aspect 10.18 against the stated 441.7 / 43.7 = 10.11, 0.7 percent out. Scaled on the stated width it is 2.94 px per mm across and 2.92 down. The jack pitch then reads 13.95 mm over the 20 steps inside the blocks of one row, which is the 13.97 mm of the ganged RJ45 registry entry, measured on a quantity the scale never saw. Figure 5 (g022646, 2000 x 265 px) gives a face 1733.5 px by 168.5 px, aspect 10.29, 1.8 percent out the other way, 3.92 px per mm across and 3.86 down. Positions are taken per axis on those scales, and each reads to about half a millimetre on the front and a quarter on the rear.

grounding.note: Connect Earth Ground to an EX4400 Switch - a 2-hole protective grounding terminal on the rear panel, used with 10-32 x 0.25 in screws and the lugs LCD10-10AF-L, LCD8-10AF-L or LCD6-10AF-L. The guide gives no hole spacing. The 15.0 mm spacing is measured on the render and is estimated. The render shows two bare holes, so they are drawn as dark holes on the plate and not as screws. A two-hole lug is the seat of a pair of holes, and the library has no pair part for 10-32 holes at this spacing, so no lug seat is offered.

interface-names.note: Table 114 - the CLI addresses the switch as FPC 0, the built-in ports as PIC 0 ports 0 to 23, the two rear QSFP28 ports as PIC 1 ports 0 and 1, and the extension module as PIC 2. The names are not printed on the metal, so no interfaces block is written.

mounting.note: Mounting Options and the mounting procedures - the two-post kit EX-RMK ships in the box and mounts the brackets flush with the front or along the middle of the side panels. The separately orderable EX-4PST-RMK mounts the switch flush with the front posts of a four-post rack or recessed inside it. EX-WMK is a wall kit. No ear distance in millimetres, no rack depth range and no bracket drawing that can be measured is in the guide, so the positions are named without a number and no kit is listed. The library holds no rail kit yet.

port-leds.note: Figure 50 and Table 43 and Table 44 - each jack has two lamp windows, "1 Link activity LED" at the left and "2 Status LED" at the right, in both rows. The link activity lamp is green: steady for link without traffic, blinking for traffic, unlit for no link. The status lamp shows one port parameter at a time, chosen with the mode button: speed (SPD), duplex (DX), administrative enable (EN) or PoE (POE). The jack part names its lamps led-a (left when unrotated) and led-b. The upper row is rotated, so left and right swap there. A single mapping for the group would be wrong for one row, so the part keeps its default vocabulary and this note holds the meaning. See the gap port-lamp-vocabulary.

port-numbering.note: Figure 50 (g022608) at high zoom - under each column, one pair of printed numbers, an even number with an up arrow and the next odd number with a down arrow ("0 up 1 down", "2 up 3 down" to "22 up 23 down"). The arrows point at the port of each number, so the upper jack of a column has the even number. Numbering starts at 0, as printed. CLI names (ge-0/0/0 and so on) are not printed on the metal, and Table 114 gives PIC 0 as the built-in ports 0 to 23. The legend position and arrow spacing are estimated from Figure 50 and the render.

ports.note: Figure 4 and Figure 6 - 24 RJ-45 ports in two rows of 12, in two blocks of six columns with a gutter between them. Cells sit on the registry's 13.97 mm ganged pitch. The first cell's left edge is at 7.95 mm, the block step is 89.26 mm (so a gutter of 5.44 mm), the upper cells start at 9.5 mm and the lower at 24.05 mm (row step 14.55 mm). Each block is a single silver plate, 87.1 mm wide, 5.71 mm from the left edge for the first, drawn as decor because the metal strip is panel and not part. Counts confirmed by Table 9 and Table 114 (PIC 0, 24 ports).

power-supplies.note: THE DEFAULT SUPPLY IS 1050 W, NOT 550 W. Table 8 ships the 24P with a 1050 W AC supply, and Table 10 lists 1600 W AC as optional. The 550 W supplies are listed only for the 24T, 24X, 48T and 48F. The guide's rear render (Figure 5) shows the rear of the 24T and 24P with two supplies and does not tell the ratings apart. This device ships one supply and a cover on the second slot, as Figure 7 and Table 105 show. The text says to install no supply of a different rating in one chassis, which a bay cannot say.

rear.note: Figure 5 and Figure 7 (g022646, g022559) measured on the render, per axis, from the rear left edge (the chassis right side as seen from the front). CON jack centre 18.35, 13.6; MGMT jack centre 39.6, 13.6, both with the contact comb up; USB-A at 55.0, 12.5, vertical; RESET pinhole at 55.3, 24.9; ground plate 27.8 to 61.7 across and 27.6 to 39.7 down with two threaded holes 15.0 apart at 39.5 and 54.5; QSFP28 cages centred at 75.5 across and 14.5 and 28.2 down, labelled 0 and 1 to their left; two columns of lamps at 89.4 and 94.3 across, two for each cage per row; ESD socket at 101.1, 36.0. Fan module slots are at 108.2 and 206.0 across, and power supply slots at 255.0 and 346.4 across, each with a fan or power icon and its number above the slot or beside it. All of these are estimated from the render, to about 0.3 mm.

rear-labels.note: Figure 7 callouts 1, 6, 10 and 15 are the serial number ID label, the CLEI code label, the power supply rating label and the claim code label. They are stickers, not metal, so each is a named region and is not drawn. The render shows them as blank plates, white for three and slate for the rating label. The guide shows no content, and none is invented.

rj45-orientation.note: Figure 50 - upper-row jacks have their contact comb at the bottom and their lamp windows at the top corners, so they carry rotate 180. Lower-row jacks have the comb at the top and the lamps at the bottom corners, the default turn of the part. This is the stacked mirror the registry describes.

sources.note: EX4400 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, PDF created 2026-07-22 (331 pages). Taken from it - Table 7 to Table 10 and Figures 4 to 7 (EX4400-24P), Table 38 to Table 40 (chassis, fan and supply sizes), Tables 41 to 51 (lamps), Table 53 to Table 58 and Table 63 to Table 64 (power supplies and PoE budget), Table 52 (heat), Table 93 (environment), Table 105 (what ships), Table 114 (CLI names), and the mounting procedures. Figures 4 and 5 (g022642, g022646) are renders of the real product and are the pictures measured here. The HPE datasheet a00150783enw (Juniper's own address redirects to it) was tried once and did not answer. The community NetBox elevations of the EX4400-48F were used only to cross-check the rear counts and positions. Juniper's image library (www.juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/images/us/en/image-library/ex-series/) answered for ex4400-24x/ex4400-24x-front-high.jpg only (a JPEG, 1500 x 236). The same pattern for the 24T, 24P, 48T and 48P (front-high and rear-high, each once) and ex4400-24x rear-high all returned an HTML 404 page. So there is no studio photograph of the 24P in the sources, and the guide's renders are the only picture of each face. The 24X photograph confirms the colour and finish of the face, the status block and the extension module cover. An end-of-life search made 2026-10-20 found no end-of-life or end-of-sale notice for the EX4400 line, so the lifecycle is none-announced. The one aggregator that lists an EX4400 model shows it as supported with no date.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md) - a belly-to-belly pair is the upper cage upright and the lower turned 180, so both bails face outward. The two rear QSFP28 cages are stacked this way and the render at 3.9 px per mm does not resolve which way the latches point, so the rule decides and a photograph overturns it.

status-block.note: Figure 6 callouts 2 to 5 and Figure 54 (g022614), measured on the render of Figure 4. A dark plate 361.2 to 439.5 across and 1.4 to 15.5 down. The model name EX4400 PoE++ is at the left (the render prints PoE++ in orange). The USB-C console port is centred at 393.7, 8.3 with the USB symbol below it. Two columns of lamps sit at 406.2 and 410.1 across: SYS, ALM, MST and CLD on the left with their legends, and SPD, DX, EN and POE on the right. The rows are at 3.8, 6.8, 9.7 and 12.8 down; the render scatters them by up to 0.5 mm and they are aligned. The mode button is a flush disc at 423.1, 8.6. The legends' type size is estimated.

vents.note: The front has a hexagon punching in a band over and under the port blocks, from the logo to the status block, and none in the middle. The rear punching is two small fields above and below the QSFP28 cages. The fields are drawn as a repeating pattern in simplified outlines, not hole for hole.

width.note: Table 38 gives the chassis 17.39 in (44.17 cm) wide, and says the outer edges of the front mounting brackets extend the width to 19 in (48.2 cm). The face is the body between the folds, 441.7 mm, with no ears drawn. Height is 1.72 in (4.37 cm), 1RU. Depth is 15.71 in (39.9 cm) with no supply, fan module or extension module fitted, 16.93 in (43 cm) with a supply and fan modules, 17.35 in (44.07 cm) with an extension module as well. The bare figure 399.0 mm is carried as the chassis depth, because every module is its own part. The other two are in attrs.
